Endocrinology · published research

Pancreatic duct regeneration

Summary of the Evidence

One randomized preclinical study assigned 20 Wistar rats with or without streptozotocin-induced diabetes to three study groups. It evaluated pancreatic histology, insulin tolerance, and tissue glycogen after near-infrared LED exposure. This is one animal experiment, with no duplicate report or independent replication identified for this category (Tatmatsu-Rocha et al. 2017).

Human and clinical evidence

No human study directly examining pancreatic duct regeneration after PBM was identified. The rat findings do not establish that the same tissue response occurs in people.

Animal evidence

The study applied LED treatment over the pancreatic projection on five consecutive days and assessed the animals after 30 days. Histological duct and islet regeneration differed across groups (p = 0.001), and insulin-tolerance testing showed a between-group difference (p = 0.03). PBM-treated diabetic rats also had higher liver and gastrocnemius-muscle glycogen than untreated diabetic rats. These outcomes show tissue and metabolic differences in one chemically induced diabetes model; they do not demonstrate durable endocrine recovery or functional beta-cell formation (Tatmatsu-Rocha et al. 2017).

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The experiment used an 805-nm LED at 40 mW. Each exposure delivered 0.88 J over 0.196 cm², equivalent to about 4.49 J/cm², for 22 seconds. Treatment was applied over the pancreas once daily for five consecutive days. Only one wavelength and dose schedule were tested, and external illumination of a rat abdomen does not establish how much light would reach the human pancreas.

Interpretation

The study provides a favorable preclinical signal for pancreatic duct and islet regeneration and glucose-related metabolic measures. Confidence remains very low because the evidence comes from one small animal experiment without independent replication. Human benefit, durability, and the functional significance of the histological changes remain untested.

Certainty of evidence (estimate)

Pancreatic duct and islet regeneration and metabolic outcomes in diabetic rats: very low certainty. The findings come from one animal experiment without independent replication or human evidence.

Rationale for the certainty assessment

One randomized experiment in 20 diabetic rats reported more pancreatic duct and islet regeneration, a different insulin-tolerance response, and higher liver and skeletal-muscle glycogen after PBM. The findings are favorable but come from one chemically induced diabetes model without independent replication or human evidence. The certainty estimate therefore remains very low.
